newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 26.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 26.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** The domestic corporate sector had a mixed year of dividend payment in fiscal 1995/96 (April-March), the Business Standard reports.
A recent study revealed the private corporate sector paid 37.97 billion rupees by way of dividend in 1995/96, up 24.6 percent from 30.46 billion rupees in 1994/95, the paper says.

** The Disinvestment Commission has engaged the services of Crisil, Care and Icra to study the 40 public sector units (PSUs) referred to it by the core group of secretaries for possible disinvestment by the government, the Economic Times says.

The paper quoted Commission chairman G.V. Ramakrishna as saying that the three credit rating firms had each been allotted different PSUs and they would analyse the units with reference to future profitability, technology levels and other relevant details.

** Liquor major Shaw Wallace whose top officials are facing charges of violating the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) is seeking to raise $150 million from the issue of a Global Depository Receipt, (GDR) the Observer says.

The proceeds from the GDR issue will be utilised to part finance upgradation and modernisation of the existing units including those acquired in distilleries, breweries and the electronics business, the paper reports.
** Many Indian stock markets were closed for Christmas holidays beginning Wednesday. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), the country's premier bourse, re-opens on January 1.
On Tuesday, stocks ended mixed with the Christmas holiday mood ahead limiting activity in many dealing rooms. The 30-share BSE index .BSESN dropped 7.84 pts to 3,085.20.
The Bombay index is down one percent year-on-year from 3,110.49 on December 22, 1995 the last trading day of last year.

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) will open for trade on Thursday, close on Friday and re-open on December 31. Bolstered by heavy short-covering in select stocks, the 50-stock NSE index .NSEI rose 2.05 points to 884.05 on Tuesday.
